title: Sixth Word Conclusion Ease Of The Sale Lawful Bounds And Servanthood

questions.question: According to the passage, why is this “sale” not hard to do?
questions.answer: Because what Allah allows is wide and enough for people, and His forbidden limits do not need to be crossed.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the duties Allah has placed on people?
questions.answer: They are not many, and they are easy to carry.

questions.question: How is serving Allah described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as a great honor and a deep joy.

questions.question: What example is used to explain how a person should live as Allah’s servant?
questions.answer: The example of a soldier is used.

questions.question: In what way should a person be like that soldier?
questions.answer: A person should begin actions for Allah’s sake, handle things by His command, and live by His law.

questions.question: According to the passage, how should a person move and remain still?
questions.answer: A person should act or hold back according to Allah’s permission and rules.

questions.question: What should someone do after failing to live up to this duty?
questions.answer: That person should ask Allah for forgiveness.

questions.question: Besides asking forgiveness, what else should a believer ask Allah for?
questions.answer: The believer should ask to be accepted as Allah’s servant and to be kept trustworthy with what Allah has entrusted to him until death.

questions.question: What main question is raised at the start of the passage about giving the trust back to Allah?
questions.answer: It asks whether this duty is really difficult or too heavy for people.

questions.question: What answer is given to that question?
questions.answer: The answer is that it is not difficult at all.

questions.question: Why does the passage say people do not need to enter what Allah has forbidden?
questions.answer: Because what is lawful already gives enough room for human needs and desires.

questions.question: What does this teach about the relationship between halal and haram?
questions.answer: It teaches that halal is broad enough, so going into haram is unnecessary.

questions.question: How does the passage present Allah’s commands: as crushing burdens or as manageable duties?
questions.answer: It presents them as manageable duties.

questions.question: What feeling should a Muslim have about being Allah’s servant and soldier?
questions.answer: A Muslim should feel honored and happy about it.

questions.question: What is the simple duty given in the passage for daily life?
questions.answer: The duty is to begin actions in Allah’s name and live according to His permission and law.

questions.question: If a person makes mistakes, what attitude does the passage teach instead of hopelessness?
questions.answer: It teaches turning back to Allah with repentance and dua.

questions.question: What two requests are made in the closing supplication?
questions.answer: To be forgiven and accepted as Allah’s servants, and to remain faithful with the trust until it is taken back.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the size of what Allah has made permissible?
questions.answer: It says the lawful area is wide and sufficient.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about forbidden acts?
questions.answer: They are not needed, because lawful choices are already enough.

questions.question: How are Allah’s obligations described in terms of difficulty and number?
questions.answer: They are described as light and few.

questions.question: What comparison helps explain a believer’s role before Allah?
questions.answer: The believer is compared to a soldier serving under a commander.

questions.question: According to this comparison, what should come before a person’s actions?
questions.answer: The intention to act in Allah’s name should come first.

questions.question: What should guide a Muslim’s choices about doing something or refraining from it?
questions.answer: Allah’s permission and His law should guide those choices.

questions.question: What should a believer do immediately after recognizing a shortcoming?
questions.answer: The believer should seek Allah’s forgiveness.

questions.question: What kind of relationship with Allah is shown in the final prayer of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows a relationship of humility, dependence, repentance, and loyalty.

questions.question: In the passage, what is being denied when it asks whether the trust is too difficult to “sell”?
questions.answer: It is denying the idea that obeying Allah is an unbearable burden.

questions.question: What reason is given first to show that this duty is not too hard?
questions.answer: The first reason is that lawful things are broad and enough for people’s wants.

questions.question: What reason is given second about Allah’s commands?
questions.answer: Allah’s required duties are few and easy.

questions.question: What does the passage say is special about being Allah’s servant and soldier?
questions.answer: It is a joyful honor beyond easy description.

questions.question: What practical life rule is taught through the soldier example?
questions.answer: A Muslim should live with obedience, intention for Allah, and respect for His commands.

questions.question: How should a Muslim handle receiving and giving things according to the passage?
questions.answer: A Muslim should do both in a way that is for Allah and within His guidance.

questions.question: When someone falls short, does the passage point first to despair or to mercy?
questions.answer: It points first to mercy through asking forgiveness.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the whole passage in one sentence?
questions.answer: Living by Allah’s guidance is not too hard; it is the honorable and blessed way to use the trust He gave us.

questions.question: What misunderstanding about religion is corrected at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The misunderstanding that living by Allah’s rules is too difficult.

questions.question: How does the passage answer that misunderstanding?
questions.answer: It says the path is not heavy, because the lawful is wide and Allah’s duties are limited and gentle.

questions.question: What title-like roles are given to a believer in relation to Allah?
questions.answer: A believer is described as Allah’s servant and soldier.

questions.question: What do those roles suggest about a Muslim’s daily behavior?
questions.answer: They suggest obedience, discipline, loyalty, and acting for Allah’s sake.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should shape both action and restraint?
questions.answer: Allah’s permission and His law should shape both.

questions.question: What should happen after a person notices he has fallen short?
questions.answer: He should turn back to Allah and ask for pardon.

questions.question: What does the prayer ask Allah to do with His servants besides forgiving them?
questions.answer: It asks Him to accept them and help them guard the trust faithfully.

questions.question: How does the passage balance responsibility with hope?
questions.answer: It gives responsibility by calling for obedience, and hope by teaching repentance and dua after mistakes.

questions.question: What challenge is presented to the idea that serving Allah is too burdensome?
questions.answer: The passage challenges it by saying that serving Allah is not truly hard at all.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human desire and lawful living?
questions.answer: It teaches that lawful things are enough to meet human desire.

questions.question: Why is crossing into what Allah forbids described as unnecessary?
questions.answer: Because there is already plenty within what Allah has allowed.

questions.question: How are Allah’s religious duties described in a way that encourages believers?
questions.answer: They are described as light and not many.

questions.question: What emotional view of worship is taught in the phrase about being Allah’s slave and soldier?
questions.answer: Worship is shown as an honor and a source of deep happiness.

questions.question: What three parts of life are included in the believer’s duty in this passage?
questions.answer: Starting actions for Allah, dealing with things for Allah, and living under Allah’s permission and law.

questions.question: What should a person do if he cannot fully carry out this duty?
questions.answer: He should ask Allah to forgive his shortcomings.

questions.question: What does the final supplication show about human weakness?
questions.answer: It shows that people need Allah’s mercy and help to remain faithful.

questions.question: Until when does the prayer ask Allah to help people protect the trust?
questions.answer: Until the time when that trust is taken back from them, meaning the end of life.

questions.question: What would be a good summary of the passage for an 8th-grade Muslim student?
questions.answer: Allah’s way is not too hard, halal is enough, serving Him is an honor, and when we fail we should make tawbah and ask Him to help us stay faithful.
